title: Best Government Contracting Software in 2026: A Buyer's Guide
summary: Eight platforms compared by what they do and who they fit, from GovWin IQ to Govly.
body_markdown:
This guide covers eight platforms in alphabetical order: what each does and who it fits.


‍


**Who wrote this.** Govly wrote this guide, and Govly is one of the eight platforms. We describe the others only from their own public materials. We don't rank vendors or quote win rates we can't check, for them or for us. If anything here is wrong,[tell us](https://www.govly.com/book-a-demo) and we'll fix it.


‍


## What does "government contracting software" cover?


The label covers at least seven jobs. Most platforms do two or three well, so start by naming the job you need done.


- **Federal opportunity search.** Faster, better-filtered search over SAM.gov notices, with saved searches and alerts.
- **Contract vehicle opportunities.** RFQs issued on GWACs and IDIQs like SEWP, CIO-SP and GSA MAS. Many of these never post publicly, so you see them only if you or a partner hold the vehicle. (More on[why contract vehicle RFQs don't appear on SAM.gov](https://www.govly.com/blog/contract-vehicle-rfqs-not-on-sam-gov) .)
- **Market intelligence.** Award history: who wins what, at which agencies, for how much, and when contracts expire.
- **State, local and education (SLED).** Bids from thousands of agency sites, plus purchase-order history showing what agencies actually paid.
- **Policy and budget tracking.** Legislation, appropriations and agency budgets.
- **Proposal and pricing.** Reading solicitations, building compliance matrices, drafting responses, pricing labor.
- **Pipeline and teaming.** Tracking pursuits and working with partners on them.


A strong tool for the wrong job is wasted money. If you resell technology and your deals flow through contract vehicles, broad SAM.gov search won't show you most of them. If you write proposals all day, market data won't fix that.


‍

‍


## The eight platforms, one by one


### Bloomberg Government


**Who it's for:** Government affairs, policy and federal market research teams.


**Strengths:** Deep coverage of legislation, congressional activity, appropriations and policy news. Hard to replace if your pipeline depends on what Congress funds.


**One caution:** It's a policy service first. A contractor that mainly needs opportunities and vehicle RFQs may not use much of its news coverage.


### Contraqer (Unanet)


**Who it's for:** Value-added resellers (VARs) and other government contractors, especially teams already using Unanet.


**Strengths:** Now part of Unanet. Its[GovIntel product](https://unanet.com/contraqer) covers opportunity and partner intelligence, and GovChannel gives VARs distributor pricing, quoting, order fulfillment, renewals and reporting in one place.


**One caution:** Unanet's product page doesn't detail coverage of contract vehicle RFQs such as SEWP, so ask how those reach you. Also check how it's packaged with Unanet's CRM and ERP.


### Deltek GovWin IQ


**Who it's for:** Larger capture teams that want deep historical opportunity and award data across many agencies.


**Strengths:** A long track record, broad federal coverage, and research content alongside the data.


**One caution:** Expect a sales process before you can try it, and check which modules your team will actually use.


### GovDash


**Who it's for:** Capture and proposal teams that write a high volume of bids.


**Strengths:** One workflow for capture, proposal development, pricing and contract management, with Microsoft 365 add-ins and MCP connectors.


**One caution:** It's built for working the bid more than finding it. Many teams pair it with a separate opportunity or market data source.


### Govly


**Who it's for:** OEMs, distributors and resellers (VARs) selling to federal and SLED buyers, especially through contract vehicles.


**Strengths:** Opportunities from 40+ contract vehicles, including SEWP and CIO-SP, through your own or partners' vehicles, alongside federal and SLED solicitations. Shared workspaces for teaming, AI agents and workflows, and integrations with Salesforce and Unanet plus an API. SOC 2 compliant.


**One caution:** Vehicle RFQs are visible through vehicles you or your partners hold, so the value depends on your channel. Teams that need deep SLED purchase-order history may want a SLED data specialist alongside it.


### GovSpend


**Who it's for:** Vendors whose revenue is mostly state, local and education.


**Strengths:** SLED purchase-order and spending data that GovSpend says it collects[directly from agencies](https://govspend.com/govspend-platform/govspend-data/) , plus federal data through its Fedmine platform.


**One caution:** Its depth is in SLED. Federal-first teams and resellers working contract vehicles should check how well it covers that work.


### GovTribe


**Who it's for:** Small teams tracking federal opportunities and awards.


**Strengths:** Opportunities, awards, agency activity and vendor profiles in one search.


**One caution:** State and local coverage and some AI features are separate options. Confirm they're included if you need them.


### HigherGov


**Who it's for:** Solo consultants and small businesses.


**Strengths:** Federal, SLED and grant opportunities, forecasts, award data, labor pricing, a built-in CRM, and API and MCP access.


**One caution:** If more than one person will use it, check which plan includes shared pipelines and team workflows.


‍


## How do you choose?


If you are… Start by looking at


A solo consultant or new small business SAM.gov search first, then HigherGov or GovTribe


An OEM, distributor or reseller selling through contract vehicles Govly, which covers vehicle RFQs that broad search tools often miss


A large prime with a capture and research team Deltek GovWin IQ, often alongside a proposal tool like GovDash


A vendor selling mostly to state, local and education buyers GovSpend for purchase-order history; check SLED bid coverage in any tool you compare


A proposal team writing many bids GovDash, paired with a data source for finding opportunities


A policy or government affairs team Bloomberg Government


Many teams use two tools: one to find opportunities and one to work them.


### Questions to ask every vendor


- Which sources does it cover: SAM.gov only, contract vehicles, state and local sites, or all of them?
- Can I test it on my own products, NAICS codes and target agencies instead of a scripted demo?
- How often is the data refreshed, and how quickly do new solicitations appear?
- Does it connect to my CRM, and who owns my data if I leave?

## FAQ: government contracting software


- **What is the best government contracting software?** It depends on the job. GovWin IQ suits large capture teams, HigherGov and GovTribe suit small federal contractors, GovSpend suits SLED-focused vendors, GovDash suits proposal teams, Bloomberg Government suits policy teams, Contraqer (now part of Unanet) suits resellers that want quoting alongside market intelligence, and Govly suits OEMs, distributors and resellers selling through contract vehicles.
- **What's the best software for finding contract vehicle opportunities like SEWP or GSA MAS?** Many RFQs on GWACs and IDIQs aren't posted on SAM.gov, so general search tools miss them. Govly is built for this. It surfaces opportunities from 40+ contract vehicles through your own or partners' vehicles.
- **Do I still need SAM.gov if I buy software?** Yes. SAM.gov registration is free and required to win federal awards. Commercial tools read from it; none replace it.
